title: Filtered coherent sections and cofinal evaluation
statement: Use the universes, smallness, compactness and filteredness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and the coherent functors, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Use cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], with the same horn and edge lifting conditions over arbitrary simplicial bases. Let $\lambda<\kappa$ be infinite regular cardinals, with $\kappa$ uncountable and $\mu^\nu<\kappa$ for all $\mu<\kappa$ and $\nu<\lambda$. Let $X$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and let $q:Y\to X$ be a cocartesian fibration. Suppose every fiber $Y_x$ is $\kappa$-filtered and admits colimits of every $\kappa$-small $\lambda$-filtered diagram, and every edge transport $Y_x\to Y_{x\prime}$ preserves these colimits. Then the quasicategory $\Gamma(q)=\operatorname{Fun}_{/X}(X,Y)$ of all sections is $\kappa$-filtered. For every vertex $x\in X$, evaluation $\Gamma(q)\to Y_x$ is cofinal: for every $y\in Y_x$, the coherent comma category of pairs $(s,y\to s(x))$ is weakly contractible. No bound on the size of the total space Y or of its fibers beyond the fixed larger universe is imposed, and sections are not required to preserve cocartesian edges.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.2, printed pp. 432-434; its hypotheses (i)-(iv), both conclusions (1)-(2), and the comma-category argument in its proof. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent section theorem.

proof.text: We first record the small horn-completion construction used below. If $H$ is $\kappa$-small and $H\to C$ maps into a quasicategory, attach one $\Delta^n$ along each inner horn $\Lambda_i^n\to H$, choosing its image in $C$ by the horn-filling property. Repeat countably and take the union. The result $H\hookrightarrow\widehat H\to C$ has $\widehat H$ a quasicategory, and the inclusion has the left lifting property against every inner fibration: solve successive horn lifts and take their unions. It is a categorical equivalence by the lifting/model classes of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. It adds no vertices. At each round there are fewer than $\kappa$ finite horn diagrams; the countable union remains $\kappa$-small because $\kappa$ is uncountable regular, using the smallness convention of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. All choices concern the small source, not a bounded subcategory of $C$.

source.place: 5.4.4.2, opening reduction via 5.4.1.2 and the completion of K(α) at successor stages; read online, not archived

proof.text: Apply Step 1 to $X\to *$, obtaining $i:X\hookrightarrow X'$ with $X'$ a $\kappa$-small quasicategory. Use the opposite of clause (2) of [lem-coef-cartesian-base-equivalence-invariance] to extend $q$ to a cocartesian fibration $q':Y'\to X'$ up to fiberwise equivalence over $X$. Its model-structure and Quillen-adjunction hypotheses, in the containing universe of $Y$, are precisely supplied by [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model], including the cocartesian dual, the fiberwise criterion, and the marked inverse up to coherent equivalence. These inverse maps over $X$ induce inverse equivalences on ALL section categories by postcomposition. Restriction $\Gamma(q')\to\Gamma(i^*q')$ is also an equivalence: for any simplicial monomorphism $U\hookrightarrow V$, a lifting problem for this restriction is a lifting problem for $q'$ against $i\mathbin\square(U\hookrightarrow V)$. This pushout product is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], so the lift exists. Thus restriction has the right lifting property against all monomorphisms and is a trivial fibration in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The same pushout-product argument, using an inner horn and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow X$, proves that the section simplicial set of any inner fibration over $X$ is a quasicategory. These comparisons commute with evaluation at every old vertex. To check compatibility with transport on an old edge, pull back both fibrations and their marked comparison to that edge $\Delta^1\to X$. Their total spaces are quasicategories, because their maps to $\Delta^1$ are inner fibrations. The comparison preserves cocartesian lifts; [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] identifies each chosen lift with the image of the other by the equivalence between initial objects in its lift category. These comparisons are coherent: [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says the full subcategory of initial objects is contractible. Thus the fiber equivalences intertwine the old edge transports up to coherent equivalence. Composing a diagram, a cocone and its mapping-space universal property with inverse fiber equivalences now transfers filteredness, existence of the stipulated colimits and preservation of them. There are no new vertices in $X'$; every new edge is a composite of old edges, since a two-dimensional inner-horn attachment adjoins its composite edge and higher horns add no edges. For each newly attached composite edge, the two preceding cocartesian lifts compose to a cocartesian lift by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]; its initial-lift comparison identifies the resulting transport with the composite of the preceding transports. Induction over the horn-completion rounds therefore proves preservation for every new edge. We may work over the quasicategory $X'$ and transfer the two conclusions back through the displayed section and fiber equivalences. Rename it $X$ and its total space $Y$.

proof.text: We prove the following extension property, from which both conclusions will follow: every map $f:K\to Y$ with $K$ $\kappa$-small extends over $T(K)=K\star_X X$, with its structural map to $X$ and its original restriction on $K$. The relative join and its functoriality are [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]; put $a=qf$. By Step 1 enlarge $K$ over $Y$ to a $\kappa$-small quasicategory $K_0$. It suffices to construct the extension after this enlargement, since $T(K)\to T(K_0)$ restricts to the given map on $K$. We inductively construct monomorphisms of $\kappa$-small quasicategories over $Y$, $K_\alpha\hookrightarrow K_{\alpha+1}$ for $\alpha<\lambda$. At a nonzero limit stage $\beta<\lambda$, take the union; every finite inner horn lies in some earlier quasicategory and therefore has a filler in that union. This also describes the final union at $\lambda$.

proof.text: Let $K_\infty=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}K_\alpha$ and $f_\infty:K_\infty\to Y$ be the union. Since $\lambda<\kappa$ and $\kappa$ is regular, $K_\infty$ is $\kappa$-small. It is a quasicategory by the finite-horn argument in Step 3. Each $L_x=K_\infty\times_X X_{/x}$ is a quasicategory because its projection to $K_\infty$ is the pullback of the right fibration of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]; horn lifting is preserved by degreewise pullback. Its total simplices number less than $\kappa$. For any $\lambda$-small $A$ and $A\to L_x$, the component into $K_\infty$ factors through a single $K_\alpha$: fewer than $\lambda$ nondegenerate simplices have been specified, their images occur at fewer than $\lambda$ stages, and regularity of $\lambda$ bounds these stages below $\lambda$. The given slice component then gives $A\to K_\alpha\times_X X_{/x}$. Step 4 supplies a cone at stage $\alpha+1$, which lies in $L_x$. This includes the empty $A$ and proves $\lambda$-filteredness exactly as defined in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category].

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-relative-cylinder-extension] to $K_\infty\to X$, $q:Y\to X$ and $f_\infty$. For every $x$, its shape $L_x$ is $\kappa$-small and $\lambda$-filtered by Step 5. Every fiber $Y_z$ admits all such colimits and every transport preserves them, by the assumed colimit existence and transport preservation for $q$; thus all pairs $(x,z)$ in the cited lemma are covered. It produces $F_\infty:T(K_\infty)\to Y$ over $X$, agreeing exactly with $f_\infty$. Restrict along the relative-join map $T(K)\to T(K_\infty)$ from [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. We obtain $F:T(K)\to Y$ over $X$ with $F|_K=f$. This proves the extension property of Step 3, with no bound on $Y$.

proof.text: Let $Z$ be $\kappa$-small and $d:Z\to\Gamma(q)$ be a diagram. By the definition of sections, it corresponds to $f:Z\times X\to Y$ over $X$. Its domain is $\kappa$-small: both factors have fewer than $\kappa$ total simplices and $\kappa$ is uncountable regular. Apply the extension property to this $f$. There is a simplicial map $Z^{\triangleright}\times X\to T(Z\times X)$ over $X$: on an $n$-simplex, take the initial block of vertices belonging to $Z$ as its map into $Z\times X$ and retain the entire $X$ simplex; the final cone block supplies the parameter in $\Delta^1$. The relative-join formula of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join] gives precisely these data, including empty blocks. Composition with $F$ and currying gives a cone $Z^{\triangleright}\to\Gamma(q)$ extending $d$, with apex the section $F|_X$. Its induced coherent cocone is obtained using the map $Z\times\Delta^1\to Z^{\triangleright}$, which collapses the last end to the cone vertex. For $Z=\varnothing$ the same construction yields a section. By [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], $\Gamma(q)$ is $\kappa$-filtered.

source.place: 5.4.4.2, first specialization K=Z × X; read online, not archived

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and $y\in Y_x$, and let $Z\to(y\downarrow\operatorname{ev}_x)$ be a diagram with $Z$ $\kappa$-small. Its data are $f:Z\times X\to Y$ over $X$ and a coherent family $y\to f(z,x)$ in $Y_x$. Encode that family by the simplicial set $C_Z=\Delta^0\amalg_{Z\times\{0\}}(Z\times\Delta^1)$, mapped into $Y_x$ with the first end collapsed to $y$; its other end is $Z$. Form $K=(Z\times X)\amalg_{Z\times\{x\}}C_Z$ and map it into $Y$. All these pushouts are degreewise, so $K$ is $\kappa$-small, including when $Z$ is empty, when its extra point still maps to $y$. Extend over $T(K)$ by Step 6, and put $s_*=F|_X$. The edge from the single $y$ vertex of $K$ to the $x$ vertex of the last copy of $X$ gives $\beta:y\to s_*(x)$. Here is the full simplicial construction of the cone in the exact arrow-comma model. On the section component use the map $Z^{\triangleright}\times X\to T(K)$ obtained from Step 7 and $Z\times X\to K$. For the arrow component define $J:Z^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1\to T(K)$ over the constant $x$. An $n$-simplex is $(w,t)$, where $w\in(Z^{\triangleright})_n$ and $t:[n]\to[1]$ is monotone. Let $I\subseteq[n]$ be the initial block of $w$ belonging to $Z$, and put $\epsilon(i)=1$ exactly when $i\notin I$ and $t(i)=1$. This is monotone. Write $B=\epsilon^{-1}(0)$. If $B$ contains a target vertex ($t(i)=1$), then $B\subseteq I$; map its $K$ block to the class of $(w|_B,t|_B)$ in $C_Z$. If it has no target vertex, map that block to the constant simplex at the single $y$ vertex; an empty block uses the formal degree $-1$ element. Map the final block to the last copy of $X$, constantly at $x$, and retain the entire degenerate $x$ simplex as the base coordinate. These are precisely the simplex data of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. For every monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the new initial block is $\alpha^{-1}(I)$ and the new join parameter is $\epsilon\alpha$. Thus restrictions give the prescribed operators; if restriction removes all target vertices of $B$, its cylinder simplex becomes the constant $y$ simplex by the defining quotient of $C_Z$. Hence $J$ is simplicial, including all faces and degeneracies. Its $t=0$ restriction is constantly $y$; at $t=1$ it agrees with the section cone evaluated at $x$; on $Z\times\Delta^1$ it is the original cylinder family. On the cone vertex times $\Delta^1$ it is the edge defining $\beta$, with all degeneracies. Composing $J$ with $F$ therefore gives a map $Z^{\triangleright}$ into the strict arrow-comma pullback extending the given diagram, with apex $(s_*,\beta)$. In particular its triangles and all higher compatibility data retain exactly the fixed source $y$. The comma simplicial set is a quasicategory: [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] applied to $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $Y_x\to *$ says that endpoint evaluation $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Y_x)\to Y_x\times Y_x$ is an isofibration. Pull it back along $(y,\operatorname{ev}_x):\Gamma(q)\to Y_x\times Y_x$ and apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit]. This is exactly the coherent arrow-comma model in the statement. The constructed cones, including $Z=\varnothing$, prove it is $\kappa$-filtered. Enlarge the ambient universe so this comma category is small; [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula] states that every small filtered quasicategory is weakly contractible. Hence every required evaluation comma is weakly contractible. Step 2 transfers filteredness of sections back to the original simplicial base by composing diagrams and their cocones with the displayed inverse equivalences. For cofinality, the evaluation squares have equivalences on source and target. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-colimit-restriction] to compose the proved evaluation functor with the inverse section equivalence and the fiber equivalence; it states exactly that weak contractibility of all commas survives these compositions. Write $v=wue$ for this composite and $t$ for the original evaluation, with the coherent natural equivalence $\eta:v\simeq t$ supplied by the evaluation squares and the quasi-inverse data. We do not need a separate assertion identifying their strict arrow-comma pullbacks. Choose a universe $\mathcal V$ containing the section categories, fibers and comparison data, and apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test] with $\mathcal V$ as its fixed universe. The contractible commas of $v$ give condition (1): restriction along $v$ preserves every given colimiting cocone. For any diagram $D:Y_x\to\mathcal E$ and colimiting cocone $\gamma:D\to\Delta L$, the coherent transformation $D\eta:Dv\simeq Dt$ is an equivalence by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Precomposition with it gives an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\Gamma(q),\mathcal E)}(Dt,\Delta T)$ to $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\Gamma(q),\mathcal E)}(Dv,\Delta T)$ for every $T$. Naturality of $\gamma$ identifies the composite of this equivalence with the cocone comparison for $\gamma t$ with the comparison for $\gamma v$: it is the coherent equality $(\gamma t)(D\eta)\simeq\gamma v$. The latter comparison is an equivalence since $\gamma v$ is colimiting. The dual mapping-space cone criterion of the same calculus node and two-out-of-three therefore make $\gamma t$ colimiting. Thus $t$ satisfies condition (1), and condition (3) of the space-test node gives weak contractibility of its exact arrow-comma model. All indexing categories are $\mathcal V$-small; the target $\mathcal E$ may lie in a further universe as the criterion allows. This proves the cofinality assertion for the original base.
